subject: Solis Health renewal - reserve reallocation & hot-standby plan
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Nguyen <emma.nguyen@solishealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Solis Health renewal - reserve reallocation & hot-standby plan

Hi Emma,

Thanks again for the candid usage call last week. We pulled your telemetry (Q1–Q3) and put together a short recommendation to keep your latency SLOs while lowering peak over-commit exposure. Highlights below — full breakdown attached.

Summary recommendation:
- Move 40 GPUs from the existing long-tail reserve into a dedicated hot-standby tranche (30% of current committed GPUs), available for instant burst.
- Convert 20 GPUs of burst capacity into a paid reserved tranche for predictable throughput during your nightly batch and daytime peak windows.
- Maintain a 10% buffer (auto-burst) to absorb sudden inference spikes; Redwood will monitor and auto-fallback to compatible quantized variants if utilization exceeds target.

Why this helps:
- Your 95th-percentile latency spikes correlate with KV-cache misses during multi-model runs; hot-standby reduces cold-start latency for those concurrent workloads.
- Current utilization data shows sustained 64% avg GPU utilization in daytime queues; reallocation reduces wasted idle on the long-tail reserve.

Cost/term impact (provisional):
- Net increase of 12 GPUs in reserved commitment (annualized) vs current baseline — projected +8% ARR for Redwood, with a proposed 10% volume discount on the incremental tranche.

Next steps:
1) I attached the solis_usage_breakdown_Q1Q3.xlsx and proposed-tranche-worksheet.csv — please confirm the windows (US-East hours) we should lock in.
2) If that looks good, we’ll prepare a short MAA amendment and a 30-day hold for the hot-standby tranche while you review procurement.

Available for a quick 20-min call tomorrow afternoon if you want to walk through the worksheet.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: solis_usage_breakdown_Q1Q3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)
Attachment: proposed-tranche-worksheet.csv (csv, 8KB)

From: Emma Nguyen <emma.nguyen@solishealth.com>

Date: 2026-10-14T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Solis Health renewal - reserve reallocation & hot-standby plan

Thanks Diego — quick questions after skimming the worksheet. Procurement looped me in for contracting.

1) Can you share the utilization window definitions used (timezone and sampling interval)? We run some late-evening batch jobs that look different from the daytime profile.
2) For the proposed 12-GPU net increase: can you show the historical token throughput that drove that number? Finance will ask for the delta cost per 10k tokens.
3) How long can you hold the hot-standby tranche before we sign (we might need 3 weeks for internal approvals)?

CCing procurement (procurement@solishealth.com) — they’ll follow with PO cadence and any required certificates.

Best,
Emma Nguyen
Director, ML Platform | Solis Health

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-15T08:07:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Solis Health renewal - re: hold size and telemetry questions

Folks — forwarding Emma’s note. Procurement asked about hold window and exact telemetry definitions. Quick plan proposal below (I’ll update the sheet):

Operational ask:
- Provide a 21-day hot-standby hold window (shorter than the 30-day we normally reserve) to reduce revenue exposure; if they sign, move the hold into the committed tranche immediately.

Sizing rationale (from telemetry):
- Sampling: 1-min buckets across model-serving nodes (US-East), aggregated by customer queue.
- Peak concurrent A100-equivalent usage observed: 180 GPU-minutes per minute during peak windows.
- Current committed baseline: 160 GPUs; daytime sustained avg utilization ~64%; spikes push to 92th percentile.
- Proposed reallocation: 40 GPUs hot-standby + 20 GPUs paid reserve conversion. This gives ~8% headroom against 95th-percentile demand and preserves burst-to-reserve economics.

Pricing suggestion (for negotiation):
- Incremental annualized commitment: +12 GPUs on the accounting baseline. Offer a 10% discount on incremental tranche + one-time credit of 2 weeks consumption applied if they convert within the hold window.

Operational caveats:
- Need Laura to confirm auto-fallback policy for quantized variants during overflow and any latency delta to communicate to customer.
- Need Ben to sanity-check the pricing concession and confirm we can apply a 2-week credit.

I’ll pivot the worksheet after you reply.

-- Diego

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-16T10:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Solis Health renewal - re: hold size and telemetry questions

Diego — quick alignment. Numbers look defensible. A couple of adjustments before we put this in front of procurement: 

- Reduce the announced hold to 21 days (agreed) but require a verbal renewal intent within 10 business days to keep the 2-week credit. That gives us runway.
- Swap 5 GPUs from the paid-reserve conversion into the hot-standby pool as a contingency for their late-evening batches (they said batch profile differs). That makes the incremental commitment +17 GPUs accounting-wise instead of +12 — show both scenarios in the worksheet.
- Pricing: 10% discount on incremental tranche is fine; ask for a 6-month micro-commit term on the hot-standby (auto-convert to reserve after 6 months if utilization justifies it) — that avoids a hard conversion if usage cools.

Laura — confirm the latency hit for quantized fallback. If it’s >12ms P95 we need to call that out and offer an SLO exception for the first 90 days.

Ben
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Nguyen <emma.nguyen@solishealth.com>, Solis Health Procurement <procurement@solishealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-19T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Updated proposal & MAA (hold for 21 days) — Solis Health renewal

Emma / Procurement —

Per our internal alignment, attached is an updated tranche worksheet (proposed-tranche-worksheet.csv) and a draft MAA-v1.docx. Key changes from the original note: 

- Hold window: 21 days. To qualify for the 2-week credit, verbal renewal intent must be provided within 10 business days.
- Sizing scenarios provided: conservative (incremental +12 GPUs) and contingency (incremental +17 GPUs with 5 GPU swap into hot-standby).
- Pricing: 10% discount on incremental reserved GPUs; hot-standby billed at a 50% reserve rate while on hold, converts to standard reserve pricing on commit.
- Auto-convert clause: hot-standby can auto-convert to a paid reserve after a 6-month micro-commit if utilization remains >70% for a 30-day rolling window.

Please see the attachments and let us know whether procurement needs any additional SOC2/billing language. If the MAA terms look OK, I can issue a formal amendment and place the 21-day hold.

Proposed next step: 20-minute call Wed 2026-10-21 at 10:00 AM ET to walk the worksheet and sign off on hold terms.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed-tranche-worksheet.csv (csv, 12KB)
Attachment: MAA-v1.docx (docx, 24KB)
